title: feat(plugin-audit, cli): os serve hands the audit sealer its crypto provider; a sealed row is amended before a migration rewrites it (ADR-0154 D3, D7)
body:
Part of #31908 (slice S9 + P3 of ADR-0154; P4, the `sys_audit_log` seal default and expiry, stays on the card)

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`os serve` 把它封存所有密钥用的同一个加密提供者交给审计封存器；一次性命令（`os audit verify`、`os migrate …`）不再启动封存器；三条改写审计行的迁移在改写已封存的行之前先写一条签名的「脱敏修正记录」，写不了就拒绝改写并计数。
- 为什么改：此前没有任何宿主把加密提供者交给 AuditPlugin，声明了 `lifecycle.seal` 的对象根本封存不了；`os audit verify` 自己还会把封存器拉起来、在输出里报错。ADR-0154 D7 要求每次改写已封存行都先留下签名记录，否则校验会把合法的脱敏读成「被篡改」。
- 风险与回滚：默认没有任何对象启用封存，所以对现有部署行为不变，唯一可见变化是 `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies` 现在保留行原有的 `updated_at`（与另两条迁移一致）。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/amendment-writer.ts`（证明叶子哈希后才签名的那段）、`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.ts`（先写修正记录、写失败则不改写）、`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`（把宿主加密提供者交给 AuditPlugin）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`，预期 2 个 describe 共 13 个用例全绿：脱敏行读作 `redacted`，无加密提供者时拒绝且行不变。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。
- 席位意见：同意落地。第二轮返工后契约复审 PASS（`150cac4b`，上轮 FAIL 6820203096 的必改项 F1–F3 与 F4、F5、F8、F11 均已关闭，无新必改）。一条性能小问题（每行重复验签）转跟进卡，在 P4 之前做。

## What changes

**S9 — host wiring, and no sealer on a one-shot boot (ADR-0154 D3, seat ruling 6795974647 (a), residual 6779459920 item 3).**

- `os serve` hands the `AuditPlugin` it composes the one crypto provider it seals every `sys_secret` row with: `new AuditPlugin({ cryptoProvider: () => hostCrypto?.provider })` in the auth-gated pair, and `hostCrypto.provider` for one that `requires: ['audit']` mounts. The pair is composed above the stack `plugins` loop and the host provider is built below it (both positions are pinned), so `AuditPluginOptions.cryptoProvider` now also takes a function, read once when the sealer starts at `kernel:ready`. The `hostCrypto` declaration moves above step 5d; its construction stays where the crypto-provider refusals pin it.
- `AuditPluginOptions.armSealer: false` keeps the sealer off. Every one-shot `AuditPlugin` in the CLI passes it: `data-migration-plugins.ts` (which `os audit verify` and the `os migrate audit-*` commands boot), `schema-migration-plugins.ts`, `plugin-trust-store.ts`, `stored-references/bind.ts`.
- Measured runtime host: `packages/runtime/src` composes no `AuditPlugin` (0 hits); the long-running host is `os serve` alone.

**P3 — the one redaction amendment writer (ADR-0154 D7).**

- `audit-seal/amendment-writer.ts` (`RedactionAmender`): before a row of a sealed object is rewritten, it finds the checkpoint that lists the row, opens that checkpoint's seed, rebuilds the row's leaf (under any redactions already written for it), and only when the leaf equals the leaf hash the checkpoint signed does it draft one amendment per changed value column: the checkpoint's sequence, row, column, the commitment the checkpoint sealed, the commitment of the rewritten value under the same salt, and the migration. `write()` signs each under the S1 key-id loop, stores it in `sys_audit_amendment`, and hands it to the sink (best-effort).
- Refused, the row left as it is: no crypto provider, a seed that does not open, a signer that cannot sign, a row that no longer matches its checkpoint (never amended, so it stays `modified`), a rewrite of a column sealed in clear. A row no checkpoint lists yet is rewritten with no amendment.
- The three migrations call it: `runLedgerCopyRewrite` (mail-body and key-material, hot and archive) and `migrateStoredMetadataBodyCopies`. Each takes an optional `seal` and reports a new `refused` count (also per table in `byObject`). The dry run decides the same way and writes nothing.
- `sys_audit_amendment` is registered and provisioned with its writer, its labels in every locale bundle (regenerated by `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write --filter=audit`).
- The CLI's `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies`, `audit-mail-bodies` and `audit-key-material` compose the crypto `os serve` seals with (`utils/audit-redaction-seal.ts`, over `oneShotCrypto`, as `os audit verify` does), pass the host's `audit.checkpointSigner` / `audit.checkpointSink` when registered, print refused rows per table, and exit `1` when any row was refused.
- `migrateStoredMetadataBodyCopies` now writes under `preserveAudit` with the row's stored `updated_at`, as its two siblings already did: a moved `updated_at` is a clear sealed column, so an amended row would still read `modified` (measured on the live test before the change).

## Why

No shipped host passed `cryptoProvider`, so nothing could be sealed and the sealer's own fix line could not be followed (residual S9). Once a host passes it, a one-shot boot would also start the sealer and write checkpoints during a read-only `os audit verify` (ruling 6795974647 (a)). D7 requires every rewrite of a sealed value column to write a signed amendment first, or refuse.

## Tests

- `plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts` (new, real kernel over SQLite wasm with an `archive` datasource, `sys_audit_log` sealed with its three value columns, the plugin's own sealer, the three real migrations, `verifyAuditLedger`):
  - a dry run decides and writes no amendment and no row;
  - no crypto provider: the sealed copy is refused (`refused` 2, the warn line names the row), left as it is; the unsealed copy is rewritten with no amendment; verify stays clean;
  - a signer that cannot sign: refused at the write, row unchanged, no amendment;
  - a sealed copy changed outside the platform: refused, never amended, verify reads it `modified`;
  - mail-body, key-material and metadata-body rewrites each amend: verify reads `redacted`, `rewritten_by` names the migration;
  - the archive run amends a copy the archive holds: `redacted`;
  - a second rewrite of a redacted column names the commitment the checkpoint sealed and still reads `redacted`;
  - `armSealer: false` starts no sealer, whatever crypto provider it is handed.
- `cli/src/commands/audit/verify.integration.test.ts` 3d: a due, unsealed row stays unsealed through every `os audit verify` run, the checkpoint count is unchanged, and no run's stderr mentions `AuditSealer`.
- `cli/src/commands/serve-audit-registration.contract.test.ts`: the serve construction carries exactly the host crypto provider (no config-derived options, the #9863 ruling's substance kept), the resolver branch hands it too, and every `AuditPlugin` the CLI builds outside `os serve` passes `armSealer: false`.
- `cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts`: each command composes the seal into its boot, passes it to every run, and exits non-zero on a refused row.

Existing assertions changed: the registration pins in `audit-plugin.test.ts` (seven objects, the "not registered before its writer" case removed), `bundle-ownership.test.ts` (`sys_audit_amendment` owned), plugin-security's `default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts` (`sys_audit_amendment_none` declared at birth, as P1b-1 did for the other two), and the exact-report pins in `mail-log-body-migration.test.ts` / `key-material-copy-migration.test.ts` (`refused: 0`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Clause-②: `yes (widening)`** (seat ruling OQ1, release 6822031110; the changeset carries the same line). Published faces that widen, all at `patch`: `AuditPluginOptions` (`armSealer`, a function-valued `cryptoProvider`), the three migrations' options (`seal`) and reports (`refused`, total and per table), the registered `sys_audit_amendment` object with its `get` / `list` doors, and the `os migrate audit-*` JSON reports and exit code. Nothing accepted today is refused. Reviewed at `TIER_DEFAULT`: FAIL 6820203096 at `06ca6d0d`, then PASS at `150cac4b` (record on this PR).
- The census (`content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`, `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`) gains the writer's engine write site (307 → 308), regenerated by `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`; the six hand-written prose figures the gate holds were updated (307 → 308, 93 → 94 undecidable, 172 → 173 decidably elevated).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/README.md`: the registered-objects sentence (six → seven), made false by this PR.
- Residuals, not built here: an app that puts its own `AuditPlugin` in `plugins` supersedes the CLI's instance, so it carries no host crypto provider (and on a one-shot boot that composes the host stack, no `armSealer: false`); a migration run while `os serve`'s sealer seals the same window can rewrite a row the sealer seals between the decision and the write (the row then reads `modified`); `packages/spec`'s `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` comment still says `sys_audit_amendment` is unregistered (out of this slice's surface).

## Verification

Round 2 (the rework to `150cac4b`, which adds the trusted-key admission of stored checkpoints and amendments, the row-id checkpoint lookup and the single `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT` read; the live suite now has 13 cases) is reported in dev report 6821958333 on #31908, and CI is green on `150cac4b`:
